category_story: mlp0's global scope is rare multi-token word-PIECE continuation: che[wed], Philadelph[ia], well-circum[scribed], right-[hander], Smugg[ler], W[ishers]. It completes the tail subword of an already-started rare/compound word or name. Notably 10% of positions are HURT by keeping mlp0 (frac_lt_-0.5), i.e. it also actively interferes at some positions -- a messier, more mixed role than mlp1's near-purely-positive table.
local_global_match_note: Partial mismatch, flagged explicitly per wave-1 lesson. mlp0's own top-30 hurt examples are all subword continuations that complete the REMAINDER of a word already in progress (e.g. 'right-' -> 'hander') -- not one example has a bare hyphen/glue-punctuation as the target itself. This datapoint's target is exactly that glue punctuation ('brother-in' -> '-', the hyphen that opens '-law'). The categories are adjacent (both about specific/rare compound-word construction, both operate right after a hyphen appears in nearby context) but not the same task -- mlp0's headline role is 'finish this word', not 'insert this hyphen'. Calling this a mismatch rather than forcing a match.
surprises: mlp0 (1.04 nats), not mlp1 (0.30, the sampler's filter target), is by far the dominant component here -- a reminder that filtering only on mlp1's dCE can still leave a different, even larger, MLP-table effect (mlp0) unexamined.
